videos.why: A billionaire's real face, his name and a $1 salary in frame 0, then 413M pledged shares in the second line: the 'billionaires borrow, never sell' format that gave us our best Short.
strengths: Real photo bobblehead of Larry Ellison with name plate in the first frame
Second line is a bigger surprise (413M pledged, up from 346M)
Core big-money format with proven demand (281K-view breakout)
risks: 'Until last year' is only true for a 2026 upload
Oracle is less of a household name than Ellison's peers

videos.why: I put it well above rank's 5.1. Everyone everywhere uses Amazon, and 'the profit comes from rented computers, not your parcels' is a how-it-works surprise in the owner's favourite how-they-make-money format. Rank's minus points come only from the versus shape's thin record with us.
strengths: Amazon logo and $45.6B on the server-rack counter in frame 0
A clear mechanism: 18% of sales, 35 cents kept per dollar against 11%, 57% of profit
A recognisable brand around the world, in a core format
risks: 34 s, near the top of the length band
Uses 'operating profit' and segment terms, simplified to 'profit' and 'store'

videos.why: A £45 copy that became a $450.3M Leonardo is a strong 'how is that possible' fact; I put it slightly above rank's 6.7 because the hook names the painting and the figure in frame 0, but art is a newer topic for us.
strengths: Painting, its name and the £45 tag in frame 0
Payoff lands on a surprising true figure: $50.3M in fees
Cover shows the invoice figures sharp
risks: Art is untested on the channel
The cover shows the invoice, not the painting
